rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF ABSENTEE VOTING BY QUALIFIED FILIPINOS ABROAD
rows.abstract: Any overseas Filipino in any of the following categories who is absent from the place of his voting residence in the Philippines and not otherwise disqualified by law, shall have the right to register and to vote by absentee ballot in any national,regional, or local election in the city or municipality where he last resided prior to his departure from the Philippines. rows.author: C122
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09275) enacted on 2004-03-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE WATER POLLUTION CONTROL POLICY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Though the importance and necessity of maintaining our water resources is recognized, the same is not being done. Water pollution still remains prevalent and is the continuing major cause of the degradation of our marine and freshwater resources. Lack of regulation and monitoring capabilities on the part of the government contribute to the problem of water pollution. In Metro Manila, tons of garbage and septic wastes are generated and flushed to the different water channels while chemical wastewater from big factories remain untreated. Water tables and aquifers are imperiled as water pollution worsens, coupled by water wastage.> In this bill, local government units will establish area-specific effluent limitations, subject to thhe national standards established by the Environmental Management Bureau (EMB), the latter being mandated to have jurisdiction over all aspects of water quality and water pollution.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05398

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EMPLOYERS TO INFORM THEIR EMPLOYEES OF THEIR RIGHTS TO SOCIAL WELFARE BENEFITS, COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENTS OR COMPANY POLICIES UNDER EXISTING LAWS IN WRITING ON THE FIRST DAY OF THEIR EMPLOYMENT AND EVERY TIME A PARTICULAR CONTIGENCY OCCURS
rows.abstract: Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, every employer must inform his employee in writing, on the first day of his employment and every time a compensable contingency occurs, of the benefits available to the latter under existing laws, collectivebargaining agreements, company policies and practices and employment contracts, arising from employer-employ ee relationship. If the employer fails or refuses to so notify the affected employee as required herein, the employer shall be liable to payto such employee, by way of damages, the amount equivalent to the benefits which said employee would otherwise be entitled to, and without prejudice to the right of said employee from recovering the same benefits from the appropriate entity includingg his employer. For purposes of this Act, the employer, in coordination with the appropriate national agencies whenever applicable, shall conduct periodic orientation seminars.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to give highest budgetary priority to education and ensure that teaching will attract and retian its rightful share of the best available talents through adequate remuneration and other means of job satisfaction and fulfillment. In pursuance of such policy, this Act provides for the upgrading of teachers' salaries commensurate to their educational attainment and professional preparation that require them to finish a Bachelors degree and to pass the Professional Board Examination for Teachers and considering that teachers are the major components of the education process.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PRESERVE AND REHABILITATE THE FOREST BY BANNING ALL LOGGING OPERATIONS IN PRIMARY AND SECONDARY GROWTH FORESTS AND RAINFORESTS, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE A TASK FORCE FOR THE PRESERVATION AND REHABILITATION OF FORESTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROMOTION OF BIO-ORGANIC FARMING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to check the ill effects of chemical farming through the promotion of "bio-organic farming", an agricultural production system that relies on biological means of conditioning and enriching the soil under the supervision of Bio-organic Farming Commission. This Commission is envisioned to propagate bio-organic cultivation and production methods among the farmers and encourage research and development in this field of agricultural production. Corollary, it is intended to aid in solving problems related to industrial waste and community garbage disposal.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT TO SECURITY OF TENURE
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to correct the significant omissions and loopholes in our laws by amending relevant sections in our Labor Code. Specifically, it seeks to: (1) render the misclassificati on of regular employees into other kinds of employees as an unfair labor practice and provide penalties thereof; and (2) harmonize the laws on subcontracting and regular employment. Through these, we hope to secure and strengthen the Constitutionall y guaranteed right of our workers to security of tenure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8794 OR "AN ACT IMPOSING A MOTOR VEHICLES USERS' CHARGE ON OWNER OF ALL TYPES OF MOTOR VEHICLES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The Road Users Tax (RUT) at this time is untimely. What it can only do is fuel protests and inflame passions, all for the P1 billion it can raise in a year. Because RUT comes on the heels of the rise in oil prices and toll fees, and worsening traffic, it is akin to pouring gasoline on an already combustible mixture. In short, it is a Trojan Horse, with WB loan concealed  in its compartment. RUT is not a mere expiter that will hound future Filipinos who will amortize the loan. The RUTis another manifestation of the knee-jerk reaction of the government to write new taxes when revenue is down instead of vigorously implementing exciting ones.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE SALE, PURCHASE AND POSSESSION OF TOXIC AND HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES, INCLUDING SODIUM CYANIDE PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Toxic and Hazardous Substances Contrl Act of 2001;" Rationale: Sodium Cyanide (NaCN) is one of the most illegally used substances that cause extensive damage to our marine resources. This substance, while used in many manufacturing processes like mining, electroplating, jewelry making and other chemical manufacturing, is also used in the catching of live reef fish which gravely decimate the nation's fish breeding habitats, aqua-marine food chains, and consequently, diminish fish supply and eliminate the livelihood of our coastal populations who depend on the aqua-marine resource for their survival. The worst possible scenario is that illegal cyanide fishing and waste dumping would eventually threaten the food security of our people.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FILM DEVELOPMENT AND INCENTIVES BOARD, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The State shall promote and support the development and growth of the local film industry as a medium for the upliftment of the people's aesthetic, cultural and social values and for the better understanding and appreciation of the Filipino identity. > To achieve this end, the State shall formulate and implement policies and programs to upgrade the art and craft of film making and encourage the production of films for commercial purposes, intended for public entertainment, that seekto enhance the quality of life, examine the human condition and contribute to the dignity and nobility of the human spirit.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04644

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: Bill reconsidered on2003-12-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTBALISHING THE PRE-NEED PLAN CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The proliferation of pre-need corporations has raised questions on the industry's financial capabilities specifically on its ability to provide security to its investors and planholders. There is a need to regulate the industry to protectits investors and planholders from fraud by pre-need corporations. There is likewise a need to regulate the industry  to protect it from unscrupulous pre-need corporations who may take advantage of the good name of honest members of the industry. There is a need to provide regulatory standards within the industry to ensure a level playing field to enable potential purchasers true freedom of choice. Finally, there is a need to strengthen government's regulatory capabilities to insure that the inndustry serves its purpose, does not become a forum for abuse.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05535

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATIONS OF INVESTMENT COMPANIES
rows.abstract: "Investment Company Act of 2001." The purpose of this Act is to establish a comprehensive scheme of regulation to permit investment companies to serve their role in the capital formation process, and at the same time promote the applicaiton of fiduciary principles in the management and supervision of mutual funds and high standards of professionalism by their distributors and others who provide services to them and seek to prevent abuses and protect the interests of the public who are investorsin such companies.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'ls as per J.17;p.15( Aug. 28,2001)

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: Business for the day on 2003-12-08
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL OWNERS OR OPERATORS OF TELEVISION NETWORKS OR STATIONS  AND PRODUCERS OF TELEVISION NEWS PROGRAMS TO HAVE THEIR NEWS PROGRAMS CLOSED-CAPTION AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: All owners or operators of television networks or stations and producers of television programs are required to have their newscasts or news programs, national and regional in scope, with closed-captions in order to benefit persons with hearing disabilities. Provided, however, that the words of the closed-captioni ng will be in the language spoken in the same program.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06582

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL TOURISM POLICY AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill substantiates the State policy to (1) ensure the development of Philippine tourism that is for and by the Filipino people, conserving and promoting our heritage, national identity and sense of unity; (2) recognize tourism development as integral to the national socioeconomic development efforts to improve the quality of life of the Filipino people, receiving the appropriate attention and financial support necessary for the growth of this industry; and (3) promote a tourim industry that is ecologically sustainable by maintaining a balance between economic devleopment, environment and natural resource protection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: jt. ref'l as per j. 37; P.19

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09257) enacted on 2004-03-03
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR ADDITIONAL BENEFITS TO SENIOR CITIZENS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-FOUR HUNDRED AND THIRTY-TWO
rows.abstract: This bill proposes that inasmuch as the Municipal Federation of Senior Citizens Association has now organized themselves into a Provincial Federation of Senior Citizens Association, there is a need to establish an Office of the Senior Citizens Affairs (OSCA) in the Office of the Governor and City Mayor to be headed by a Provincial Board Member and a City Councilor, respectively. > Due to the high cost of funeral services, there is also a need to include among the privileges now enjoyed by senior citizens, a 20% discount on purchases of funderal services (on a pre-need basis) to lessen the burden of the family left behind by the elderly when he passes on.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05987

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING TO FIFTEEN PERCENT (15%) THE AMUSEMENT TAX ON GROSS RECEIPTS FROM ADMISSION FEES OF THEATERS, CINEMAS, CONCERT HALLS, CIRCUSES AND OTHER PLACES OF AMUSEMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 140 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The entertainment industry, saddled as it is with numerous and heavy taxes, is on the brink of economic collapse and loss of identity. The reduction of the amusement tax on theaters, cinemas, concert halls, circuses, and other places of amusement will encourage economic growth and efficiency of the Philippine entertainment industry, the creation of new jobs, exports, and consumers' accessibility to a wide range of new media content and services at competitive prices. It will encourage investments and innovations, including research and devleopment. It will foster competition and an increased reliance on market forces utilizing Filipino creative resources, thus contributing to the Filipino identity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2002-11-29, transmitted to on 2002-12-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-12-04
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SIXTY-NINE HUNDRED AND THIRTY-EIGHT
rows.abstract: Rationale: Cooperative devleopment plays a large role in the ultimate realization of national economic development. It is for this reason that the Constitution recognizes the indispensable role of cooperatives in Philippine development and progress.By definition, cooperatives provide individuals an opportunity to work together and share in the development of their own communities and ultimately, their own lives. Thus, there is a need for a legislative measure to insure that the laws governingthe organization and function of cooperatives truly address the needs of the people.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05206

rows.author: C067
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SYSTEM OF DISPOSITION OF SEIZED/ CONFISCATED ILLEGALLY CUT, GATHERED, REMOVED, AND POSSESSED LOGS, LUMBER, FLITCHES AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Disposition of Seized/Confiscated Illegally Cut and Possessed Logs and Other Forest Products
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to curb this anomalous situation by PROHIBITING the DENR and the NRDC from conducting a PUBLIC AUCTION on all seized and confiscated illegally cut, gathered, removed, and possessed logs, lumber, flitches and other forest products. Instead these should be donated to the local government units (LGU) with jurisdiction over the area of origin to benefit their respective communities. These will be distributed according to priority, enhancing delivery of education, housing and infrastructure in the territorial jurisdiction of the LGU concerned.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2002-05-23, transmitted to on 2002-05-28 and received by the Senate on 2002-05-28

second_reading.remarks: The Body approved to consider the Explanatory Note of the Bill as the sponsorship remarks.

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09302) enacted on 2004-07-27
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED NINETY-ONE, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE CHARTER OF THE PHILIPPINE DEPOSIT INSURANCE CORPORATION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend the charter of the Philippine Deposit Insurance Corporation (PDIC). This bill promotes and safeguards public interest by establishing the basic policy of providing permanent and continuing coverage on all insured deposits. It increases insurance coverage from One Hundred to Two Hundred Thousand Pesos, thus increasing the protection granted each depositor. It gives the PDIC the authority to review insurance ceverage every five years to give it some flexibility in its policy-determin ing functions.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06003

rows.author: C067
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING THE FISCAL INCENTIVES UNDER EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 226, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS CODE OF 1987, AS AMENDED, AMENDING PERTINENT ARTICLES OF THE CODE, PROVIDING FOR PENALTIES IN VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This proposed legislation on the rationalization of investment incentives will pave the way for an incentive system that is consolidated and highly focused, cost-effective in promoting investments time-bound and simple to administer. This rationalization is necessary in order to meet, among others, the following objectives: (1) to address the intense competition for foreign direct investment in the Asian region;  (2) to bring the country's incentive schemes in line with those in the ASEAN; and(3) to achieve harmony with the WTO agreements , particularly on subsidies and countervailing measures.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06011

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A CHAMBER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY SYSTEM, PROMOTING ORDER, EFFICIENCY, AND EFFECTIVE DELIVERY OF SERVICES BETWEEN AND AMONG CHAMBERS OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to promote the growth of chambers of commerce and indusatry (CCIs) nationwide. Presently, there is NO chamber  of commerce and industry system for all business and economic sectors. Chambers have thus uncontrollably mushroomed acrossthe country with overlapping and duplication of functions and services resulting in inefficiency, and inability to provide value-added services for their members, among others.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to EXEMPT the following services from the VAT:  (1) Services rendered by banks, non-bank financial intermediaries, finance companies and other financial intermediaries not performing quasi banking functions; (2) Services performed asactors or actresses, talents, singers and emcees; radio and television broadcasters; choreographers; musical, radio, movie television and stage directors; (3) Services performed as professional athletes; and (4) Services performed in the exercise ofprofession or calling and professional services performed by registered general professional partnership.

rows.author: B011
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVISING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FORESTRY PROFESSION LAW
rows.abstract: Rationale: Republic Act 6239, otherwise known as the Forestry Profession Law was enacted into law on 19 June 1971 and is, therefore, about 28 years old. Expectedly, its provisions include items that have outgrown their relevance to government and the 7,000 professional Filipino Foresaters in the country today.> The approval of the proposed revision is urgent and highly desirable in order to enable the professional Filipino foresters to effectively address the vaious demands of their clientele and accordingly react to social and political issues and critical environmental concerns besetting the country today. The Filipino Forester's role in sustainable development will be enhanced and the mechanism for the growth of the profession will be iinstitutionaliz ed in this porposed Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B011

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST RESOURCES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to institutionaliz e a new but theory-based management system for the country's forest resources, the Community-Based Forest Management (CBFM) strategy.  As the major strategy in forest resource management, (CBFM will pave the way for the DIRECT PARTICIPATION of some twenty million (20M) forest resident families and indigenous communities who are currently occupying the country's forestlands, as partners of the State in protecting the forest from poachers and illegal loggers andimplementing reforestation programs.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05162

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CIVIL SERVICE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed Code seeks to address the deeply-rooted problems besetting the public service, among which are: graft and corruption ; red tape; violations of employee rights, specifically the right to security of tenure and the right to due process oflaw; violations of the merit and fitness principle; partisan political activities; inadequate employee benefits and privileges; organization ineffectiveness and unnecessary delays in frontline services delivery.

rows.abstract: This bill seeks to amend Republic Act 1405 or the Bank Secrecy Law. It allows examiners only from the BSP, PDIC, to look into records of depositors and transactions of banks not only to ensure that these banks are in healthy condition, but most importantly tnat no laundered money is deposited.

rows.abstract: PLANT, MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT THAT ARE REASONABLY NEEDED AND ACTUALLY USED FOR THE PRODUCTION AND TRANSPORT OF GOODS AND SERVICES MAY BE DEPRECIATED USING A DEPRECIATION RATE TWICE AS FAST AS THE NORMAL RATE: PROVIDED, HOWEVER, THAT THIS METHOD ISAVAILABLE ONLY TO PLANT, MACHINERY AND EQUIPMENT DEPRECIATED UNDER THE STRAIGHT LINE METHOD; AND PROVIDED, FURTHER, THAT THE TAXPAYER NOTIFIES IN WRITING THE COMMISSIONER OF INTERNAL REVENUE AT THE BEGINNING OF THE DEPRECIATION PERIOD AS TO WHAT DEPRECIATION RATE ALLOWD THEREUNDER SHALL BE USED BY IT.

rows.abstract: This proposed measure seeks to adopt the following: (1) interest income derived from deposits and deposit substitutes shall be exempted from the 20% final tax; and (2) banks, finance companies and insurance premiums shall be exempted from the GrossReceipts Tax (GRT).

rows.author: C113
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE I OF BOOK II OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, ENTITLED "HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT"
rows.abstract: "National Manpower Development Act of 2001." Rationale: The absence of a national skills development plan has harmful effects on the economy because of the difficulty in dove-tailing training programs of individual agencies with the development needs of the people, industries and enterprises in the regions. For a training program to be meaningful, one should examine an area's profile so that the needs of the people, industries and enterprises at the regional, provincial, municipal and congressional levels can be addressed appropriately. The proposed amendments to the Labor Code will give new direction to the implementation of the National Skills Training Development Plan through closer supervision, coordination and monitoring of all trainiing activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C113
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN, AMENDING SECTIONS 308 AND 309 OF CHAPTER 2; SECTIONS 423, 430, 433, 434 AND 435 OF CHAPTER 8, AND SECTIONS 436 AND 437 OF CHAPTER 9, TITLE V OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Some of the provisions in RA 7160 that were amended by this bill focused on: 1) allocating a separate funding to the SK organizations and its officials, to be provided initially through the National Budget; 2) granting more powers to the SK officials especially in the management of their affairs; and 3) improving the SK's processes and procedures in its operations, thereby making the SK officials primarily responsible for their decisions and autonomous to local government unit/s concerned.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS (BSP), PHILIPPINE DEPOSIT INSURANCE CORPORATION (PDIC) AND BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE (BIR) TO LOOK INTO DEPOSITS OF ANY BANKING INSTITUTION, THEREBY AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1405, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All deposits of whatever nature with banks or banking institutions in the Philippines including investments in bonds issued by the Government of the Philippines, its political subdivisions and its instrumentaliti es, are hereby considered as of an absolutely confidential nature and may not be examined by any person, government official, bureau or office, except [upon written permission of the depositor,] BY EXAMINERS FROM THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS (BSP), PHILIPPINE DEPOSIT INSURANCE CORPORATION (PDIC), AND BUREAU OF INTERNAL REVENUE (BIR) SOLELY FOR SUPERVISORY AND TAX AUDIT PURPOSES, or upon order of a competent court in cases of bribery, or dereliction of duty of public officials, or in cases where the money deposited or invested iis the subject matter of the litigation.

rows.author: C113
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION TWENTY-SEVEN OF THE TAX REFORM ACT OF 1997 AND HEREBY IMPOSING A TAX ON INTEREST INCOME AND CAPITAL GAINS OF THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM (GSIS) AND SOCIAL SECURITY SYSTEM (SSS)
rows.abstract: Rationale: The incomes of the GSIS and the SSS, both from contributions and investments are EXEMPT from all taxes. The tax exemption of the SSS and the GSIS give them an advantage over other investment houses and pension funds when they participatein the capital market.  The tax exemption gives them higher profits in their investments and this allows them a wider room in making deals. To level the playing field, this bill proposes to tax the investment of the SSS and GSIS.  They will be subject to taxes such as capital gains tax and stock transaction tax, 20% final tax on deposits just like any other corporation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE COMMISSIONER OF CUSTOMS TO ALLOW FOREIGN VESSELS TO LOAD AND UNLOAD CARGO AND ARTICLES FOR FOREIGN TRADE AT ANY PHILIPPINE PRINCIPAL PORT AND SUBPORT (RE: CABOTAGE)
rows.abstract: This bill recognizes the need for alternative means of shipping cargoes intended for foreign trade. However, these should not adversely affect the domestic shipping industry. Thus, it is proposed that the Commissioner of Customs be given authority to clear foreign vessels to load and unload cargoes and articles intended for foreign trade in the country's principal ports and subports.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO LIBERALIZE THE OPERATIONS OF RURAL BANKS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7353, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE NEW RURAL BANKS ACT OF 1992 AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Rural banks play a crucial role in the economy since they are in the forefront of the rural financial system.  They mobilize small savings and provide farmers, fishermen, microentreprene urs, employees, market vendors and other rural workers access to credit in order to give them the opportunity to improve the quality of their life by engaging in productive activities. The Rural Banks Act of 1992 was passed in recognition of the need to make credit available and accessible in the rural areas. However, due to the rigid interpretation of the law by government agencies, the beneficial effects of RA 7353 were diluted.  This proposed bill aims to resolve the issues and plug the loopholes that diluted the real intent of RA 7353.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06533

rows.title_full: AN ACT RESTRUCTURING THE OIL INDUSTRY BY ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL OIL EXCHANGE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to establish a national oil exchange (hereinafter referred to as "OilEx") that will bid (spot market) and/or negotiate (term contracts) our country's total requirement of refined petroleum products (RPPs) such as gasoline, diesel, kerosene, LPG, etc.  Said bidding and/or negotiation shall be open to all the oil refineries and traders in the world.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2001-07-24
